title: What If It Rained in the Driest Desert on Earth?

scenes.text: What if it rained in the driest desert on Earth? Long-buried seeds would wake up.
The Atacama normally gets about 15 millimeters of rain a year, and some towns get only 1 to 3.
In March 2015, the city of Antofagasta got 23 millimeters in one day, about seven years of rain.
The storms brought floods and mudslides that killed more than two dozen people.
That October, around 200 plant species bloomed across the desert, turning gravel into pink carpets.
Scientists called it the most spectacular bloom in 40 or 50 years, and it faded by early November.
